## About these questions {.unnumbered}

These questions are for extra practice after Lab 5, using the same data.
Each section follows on from the matching task in `lab_05.qmd`, so do that task first.
Questions marked **Extension** are more challenging.

The cell below loads the data we used in the lab.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
characters <- read_csv("data/simpsons/simpsons_characters.csv")
episodes <- read_csv("data/simpsons/simpsons_episodes.csv")
locations <- read_csv("data/simpsons/simpsons_locations.csv")
script_lines <- read_csv("data/simpsons/simpsons_script_lines.csv")
stock_data <- read_csv("data/all_stocks_5yr.csv") |>
    clean_names()
```

### Joining Data

These questions follow on from Tasks 1 and 1b of the lab.
(Make sure your outputs print character names, not just IDs).

- [x] Which characters have lines in the most episodes?
- [ ] **Extension:** Which characters appear together most frequently in episodes?

::: {.solution}
This is which episode does homer have the most lines in.
```{r}
script_lines |> inner_join(characters, by = c("character_id" = "id")) |> inner_join(episodes, by = c("episode_id" = "id")) |> group_by(character_name, title) |> summarise(n_lines = n()) |> arrange(desc(n_lines))
```
Who has lines in most episodes:
```{r}
script_lines |> inner_join(characters, by = c("character_id" = "id")) |> inner_join(episodes, by = c("episode_id" = "id")) |> group_by(character_name) |> summarise(n_episodes= n_distinct(episode_id)) |> arrange(desc(n_episodes))
```


:::

### String Processing

These questions follow on from Task 2 of the lab.

- [ ] How many lines contain exclamation marks?
- [ ] **Extension:** Read about *regular expressions* (see the Regular Expressions tip in the Week 5 notes, and try [regex101](https://regex101.com/)). In the lab you counted the episodes that mention donuts / doughnuts. Answer that question again, this time using a single `str_detect` with a regular expression that matches both "donut" and "doughnut".
- [ ] Some location names are written in capitals (e.g. `KITCHEN`) and others are not (e.g. `Simpson Home`). How many are in capitals? Use `str_to_title` to give all the location names consistent capitalisation. Look through the results: does `str_to_title` always give what you want?

::: {.solution}

:::
